00088 /**
00089  * @brief               Create a dialog 
00090  *
00091  * HxDialogNew is called to create and show a modal dialog window.
00092  *
00093  * If pBounds is set to NULL, default values are used.  Default values
00094  * center the dialog in the display, and create a dialog that has a
00095  * default width and height.
00096  *
00097  * This function should be used for general purpose dialogs.  For a color
00098  * picker, use HxColorDialogNew.  For File Open or File Save [As] dialogs,
00099  * use HxFileDialogNew.
00100  *
00101  * The toolkit returns an error is the application attempts to open a dialog
00102  * with the same resource ID of a dialog that is already open.  This check
00103  * frees the application from performing the same check, provided the dialog
00104  * is not created using the kHxWidgetAutoID constant when calling HxDialogNew
00105  * (or using $AUTO in a dialog resource definition).
00106  *
00107  * @param id            IN:     Dialog resource ID
00108  * @param pBounds       IN:     Rectangle describing the position and size
00109  *                              of the dialog. If NULL, default values are
00110  *                              used.
00111  * @param pTitle        IN:     Title of the dialog, or NULL
00112  * @param hDialog       OUT:    Handle to the created dialog 
00113  *
00114  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK on success.  *hDialog is set
00115  *                              to NULL if there is an error.
00116  *
00117  **/
00118 HxResult HxDialogNew(uint32_t id, const HxRectangle_t* pBounds,
00119                         const char* pTitle, HxDialog_t** hDialog);

00203 /**
00204  * @brief               Close all open dialogs and alerts
00205  *
00206  * HxDialogCloseAllDialogs closes an application's open dialogs and alerts.
00207  *
00208  * This function is intended to be called by applications when the application
00209  * is being moved to the background (from its kHxApplicationIsDeactivated
00210  * notification callback).
00211  *
00212  * The system closes dialogs by sending a kHxCommandButtonChanged message
00213  * for the dialog's command button tagged as the "escape" button with the
00214  * HxDialogSetEscapeButton API, or with the "escape" resource attribute.  If
00215  * an escape button is not set by the application HX_MISSING_RESOURCE is
00216  * returned and the function exits without closing more dialogs. 
00217  *
00218  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK on success.
00219  *
00220  **/
00221 HxResult HxDialogCloseAllDialogs(void);

00262 /**
00263  * @brief               Set the "escape" command button
00264  *
00265  * HxDialogSetEscapeButton allows an application to indicate which command
00266  * button should be acted on when the user presses the "escape" key.  (The
00267  * "escape" key is the top left key on the keyboard, the back-quote.) 
00268  * When the key is pressed, the system sends a kHxCommandButtonChanged message
00269  * for the command button.  Normally, this command button would be "Cancel",
00270  * or its equivalent.
00271  *
00272  * If the application disables this command button, then a message is not
00273  * sent when the user presses the "escape" key.
00274  *
00275  * If the dialog has an editable field, and if the field has focus, then the
00276  * key is sent to the field rather than to the command button.
00277  *
00278  * @param pDialog        IN:    Pointer to a dialog
00279  * @param buttonID       IN:    Resource ID of the command button
00280  *
00281  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns
00282  *                              HX_NULL_POINTER if pDialog is NULL.  Returns
00283  *                              HX_INVALID_ARG if the button ID is not
00284  *                              associated with a command button in the dialog.
00285  *
00286  **/
00287 HxResult HxDialogSetEscapeButton(HxDialog_t* pDialog, uint32_t buttonID);
